title: 脳情報科学
subtitle: Brain Information Science
educationalGoal: Brain is the basis of psychological functions. The rapid development of brain research method allowed the clarification of brain functions in various psychological processing. The goal of this course is to provide students with the basic knowledge of brain functions such as “attention & eye movement”, “long/short term memory”, “Emotion and its control”, “Emotion & brain waves”, “Cognitive control & decision making”, “Social cognition” and “Theory of mind”.
advice: This course focuses on brain functions related to attention and eye movements, long-term memory and working memory, generation and control of emotion, cognitive control and decision making, sociality, and theory of mind, among various psychological information processing processes. The course aims to ensure students' understanding of the fundamentals of psychology based on brain information science and to help them acquire comprehensive learning skills. The majority of the course will be conducted in the form of lectures. Students will be given a quiz almost every week to review the content of the previous class.
requiredKnowledge: Students should have a review of Perceptual and Cognitive Psychology and Introduction to Psychology. It is desirable that students have taken Neuro-Physiological Psychology.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand brain function of various psychological processing.
Be able to understand the basis of psychology and brain science.
Be able to explain fundamental factors to construct a system that suits psychological processing.

achievementLevels.ideal: A thorough understanding of the fundamentals of psychology based on brain information science regarding information processing, including human attention and eye movements, long-term and working memory, emotions, cognitive control and decision making, and sociality, and the application of this knowledge to information design compatible with the human psychological information processing process.
achievementLevels.standard: Demonstrate an understanding of the fundamentals of psychology based on brain information science regarding information processing, including human attention and eye movements, long-term and working memory, emotions, cognitive control and decision making, and sociality, and an understanding of information design compatible with human psychological information processing processes.
